text:
maria: FYI hit a weird failure when we failed traffic to eu-west-1 replica MRK — app couldn't decrypt payloads that were encrypted in us-east-1. Anyone seen this pattern?
sanjay: Did CloudTrail show kms:Decrypt AccessDenied or something else?
maria: AccessDenied on Decrypt. Error from the app: AccessDeniedException: User arn:aws:iam::444:role/redwood-app cannot call kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abc123. We're assuming cross-account role into 111.
anya: Are you using AWS Multi-Region CMKs (MRKs) or separate keys that you manually replicated? MRKs have slightly different semantics for ciphertext IDs.
eli: Quick checklist: key policy grants, IAM principal allowed, any CreateGrant usage, and whether grants exist on the replica. Grants and key policies are per-key ARN and don't magically replicate.
maria: We're on MRKs with a primary in us-east-1 and a replica in eu-west-1. I assumed decrypt would work on replica for ciphertext generated earlier.
sanjay: In practice the principal needs permissions on the replica key as well. If the app encrypts in us-east-1, the ciphertext references the primary. Decrypt on replica fails unless policy/grants match.
sean: Also remember envelope encryption: we GenerateDataKey in primary, store plaintext-derived key wrapped (ciphertext blob) with KMS. If you try Decrypt the blob in another region and the principal doesn't have rights on that replica key, it will fail.
anya: For failover you have two options: rewrap stored data key ciphertext using the replica (Decrypt old -> Encrypt with replica) or ensure replica key policies/grants allow the same principal. Rewrapping is safer but needs access to both keys.
maria: How did this surface in prod? We had some customer requests 500 during manual failover.
eli: Look at CloudTrail -> kms:Decrypt events correlated with the app request IDs. If you see AccessDenied events spikes, you know it's key-policy/grant related. Capture the requestId and principal in the timeline.
sanjay: We should add an incident playbook section: 1) identify affected key ARNs; 2) validate replica key policies and any grants; 3) if urgent, create temporary CreateGrant on the replica for the role; 4) run a rewrap job for data keys and verify success; 5) record events to postmortem.
maria: Can infra automate grant replication when we create MRKs? I don't think AWS replicates grants.
sean: Correct — AWS doesn't replicate grants or IAM changes for MRKs. We built a small lambda in infra that copies key policies and replicates grants when a replica is created. I can open a task to run it for prod MRKs.
anya: Also add audit steps: snapshot CloudTrail logs, export key policy JSONs, and take a config snapshot of IAM roles involved. If this hits customers, loop in sec-oncall and legal.
sec-oncall: Confirmed. If customers were affected, open a P1, notify affected customers per the communication template, and include timeline & mitigation steps. Avoid rotating keys during the immediate failover; rotation can worsen decrypt issues.
maria: Regarding rotation — if we rotate while failing over, rewrap becomes harder. Best to stabilize, then schedule rotation with rewrap in controlled batches. Any tips for large data volumes?
eli: For large volumes do background rewrap in chunks and backoff. Rewrapping requires Decrypt on old key and Encrypt on new key, so ensure both keys' policies/grants permit the service account doing the rewrap. Rate limit to avoid KMS throttling.
sanjay: Another pattern: double-wrap at write time — encrypt the data key under both primary and replica keys so either region can decrypt without immediate rewrap. Storage cost and complexity tradeoffs exist but it buys faster failover.
anya: Document double-wrap as an opt-in optimization in runbooks, and call out how it interacts with rotation (you must rewrap both ciphertexts).
maria: Action items: (1) infra — run grant-replicator for our prod MRKs (sean), (2) infra/dev — add CloudTrail metric alert for repeated kms:Decrypt AccessDenied spikes (sanjay), (3) postmortem + customer comms template (maria).
kms-bot: Created INFRA-827: grant-replicator runbook task, linked MRKs: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abc123 and replica arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111:key/replica456.
maria: Thanks. I'll draft the incident postmortem in #postmortems and include the rewrap options + audit timeline.
sean: I'll prioritize the replicator run in the infra sprint and add a smoke test that simulates region failover decrypts.
maria: Great, ping me if you need a test account with cross-account roles.
sec-oncall: Also add a playbook step to check CloudTrail retention and export logs to S3 before they roll off.
maria: Will do — wrapping up here, thanks all :heart:
